new.title: The Local Star Formation Environment Predicts Young Star Cluster Radii: Evidence from PHANGS-MUSE H-alpha Maps
new.summary: The effective radii of young star clusters correlate with cluster mass, but the large scatter about that relation is not well understood. Theory predicts that a cluster's initial radius depends on the gas surface density of its natal environment, so the star formation environment should leave a measurable imprint on cluster structure. In a companion analysis of 5,105 clusters across 31 LEGUS galaxies, we found that galaxy-wide specific star formation rate (sSFR) carries no predictive power for cluster radius. Here we test whether that null result reflects the spatial scale on which the environment was measured. We cross-match the LEGUS cluster catalog of Brown & Gnedin with H-alpha maps from the PHANGS-MUSE survey in the four galaxies common to both surveys, and measure the local star formation rate surface density, Sigma_SFR, at the position of every cluster by aperture photometry. For the 325 clusters younger than 10 Myr with reliable radius and mass measurements, local Sigma_SFR significantly predicts effective radius (beta = 0.079, p = 2 x 10^-4) in a model containing mass and age, while the host galaxy's sSFR does not (beta = 0.042, p = 0.40) for those same clusters. The local model generalizes nearly three times better under cross-validation (CV R^2 = 0.061 versus 0.022). The effect operates among clusters within a single galaxy: it survives galaxy fixed effects (beta = 0.068, p = 0.001) and appears independently in each of the two galaxies large enough to fit alone. Including local Sigma_SFR also reduces the mass coefficient by 26%. The birth environment measurably shapes cluster structure, but only when it is measured on the scale on which clusters actually form.

new.title: Environmental dependence in the halo model informed by the FLAMINGO simulations
new.summary: Galaxy-galaxy lensing (GGL) measurements around galaxy samples in different environments provide valuable information about the galaxy-halo connection. In such studies the halo model is commonly used to estimate physical parameters from the lensing signal, but the impact of environment is generally not considered. Our aim is to adapt the halo model to allow a density-split GGL analysis and to understand the environmental dependence of the elements of the model. We use the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to construct samples of halos in underdense and overdense regions. Environment density is assigned to halos based on halo counts within an aperture, employing different aperture sizes to probe both local and large scales. We utilize spherical apertures with radii between $1 h^{-1} {\rm Mpc}$ and $10 h^{-1} {\rm Mpc}$. We find a strong dependence on environment for the halo mass function (HMF) and the halo bias. To account for this, we propose an empirical modification that can be applied to existing HMF prescriptions. We find that after a density split, the halo bias is approximately constant with mass. There is also an environmental dependence for the stellar-to-halo-mass relation (SHMR), the conditional stellar mass function, and the mass-concentration relation, all of which can be addressed with existing models. We evaluate the impact of overlooking environment on halo occupation distribution (HOD) parameter inference, finding that it leads to biased estimations of the SHMR and the satellite fraction. These results emphasize the need to review the assumptions adopted in the halo model when working with samples of galaxies binned by environment, and consequently, by galaxy properties that correlate with environment, such as morphology and color.

new.title: Missing Light, Misleading Confidence: Optical-Module Readout Loss and Signal Reliability in Neutrino Telescopes
new.summary: Optical neutrino telescopes reduce the photomultiplier signals of an optical module or string segment to compact multichannel summaries, and readout loss can make these summaries unreliable. We asked whether availability-based quality gates, which accept a summary when enough of the readout was live, can certify a summary of inter-channel statistical consistency (called coherence here; not optical coherence) under readout loss, and where they fail. We used public IceCube pulses (9,484 string records) and the released hits of KM3NeT event KM3-230213A with controlled readout loss, together with a replay of real KM3NeT readout flags. In a two-by-two design we compared a published recursive support state with direct mask support, and calibrated every threshold on development records. The support state is a function of the mask and added no information. On IceCube the support-gated rule retained 0.16 percentage points more usable summaries, an effect of the window at which support was read that reversed sign at a looser tolerance; on KM3NeT it accepted nothing. The gates accepted only records with nearly intact masks, including records whose charge had been depleted by signal-dependent loss that the mask does not record. Pulse loss during live acquisition and timing jitter passed every availability gate, which then accepted summaries of which up to 66% were unreliable. Availability flags are therefore necessary but not sufficient, and signal-based checks are needed. This work uses public data and is not an IceCube or KM3NeT Collaboration result.

new.title: Analysis of Binary O-type Star Systems Using Recurrent Neural Networks
new.summary: This work presents an initial analysis of the estimation of effective temperature and surface gravity for simulated O-type binary systems using a recurrent neural network. The proposed system uses 34 equivalent-width measurements from the optical region of a stellar spectrum. Two methods were applied to observed IACOB spectra before normalization: the addition of a blackbody continuum and the addition of a second observed spectrum. The first method produces only small differences in the normalized line profiles and in the estimated physical parameters over 3700-7000~Å. In the second method, the secondary spectrum is added with contributions of 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, and 75 per cent, as defined relative to the original primary spectrum. The general comparison includes 192 simulated systems and 1152 modified spectra. For most of these spectra, the estimated effective temperature and surface gravity decrease as the contribution of the secondary component increases. Individual examples using HD14947, HD190429, HD48099, and HD206267 show that this behavior is not the same for every combination: some estimated effective temperatures fall below the estimates for both isolated spectra, and some surface gravity estimates increase. Comparisons with previously published values also depend on the physical parameter and reference considered. The results show that the proposed system is sensitive to the addition of a secondary spectrum, but do not establish a unique contribution for the secondary component of an observed binary.

new.title: Multiline Spectropolarimetric Evidence for Photospheric Reconnection in Ellerman Bombs from DKIST
new.summary: Ellerman bombs (EBs) are compact, transient brightenings observed in the wings of Balmer lines and are believed to result from magnetic reconnection in the lower solar atmosphere. However, their signatures have rarely been observed simultaneously in multiple spectral lines sensitive to the lower atmosphere. We present novel high-resolution multiline spectropolarimetric observations of EBs obtained with the Visible Spectro-Polarimeter (ViSP) on the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST). Simultaneous observations reveal remarkable H$\beta$ wing enhancements extending up to $\sim$4~Å from the line core and intensity enhancements in the \ion{Na}{1}~D1 and \ion{Fe}{1}~6302 lines. Using multiline non-LTE inversion of the \ion{Na}{1} and \ion{Fe}{1} lines, we infer localized photospheric heating of up to $\Delta T\sim$800~K, accompanied by weak upflows and downflows at EB locations. Comparing with synthetic observables from Bifrost radiative-MHD simulations, we find that synthetic spectra reproduce the observed H$\beta$ and \ion{Na}{1}~D wing enhancements and yield atmospheric stratification broadly consistent with those inferred from the non-LTE inversion. This study provides strong evidence that EBs are driven by photospheric magnetic reconnection below the temperature-minimum region, and places new constraints on the realistic EB models and small-scale energy release in the lower solar atmosphere.

new.title: A Two-Population von Mises--Fisher Distribution of the Magnetic Field Direction in the Young Solar Wind
new.summary: The one-point distribution of the magnetic field direction in the young solar wind is found to be a superposition of two populations rather than a single exponential. Using Parker Solar Probe (PSP) Encounter 1 magnetometer data, we show that the distribution of the pitch-angle cosine mu(t) = bhat(t) . bhat_0 is well described by a two-component von Mises-Fisher (vMF) mixture: a broad, weakly confined component of concentration kappa_1 ~ 3.6 that accounts for the large-amplitude rotations and switchback tail, and a field-aligned component that reduces, in the small-angle limit, to a Gaussian in the polar angle theta of width sigma ~ 15 degrees (concentration kappa_2 ~ 14). The concentration of the field-aligned component is not a free parameter: it is set by the level of the transverse Alfvenic fluctuation through kappa_2 = 2<|B|^2>/<delta B_perp^2> = 2/<1-mu^2> ~ 16.2, in agreement with the fitted value to within ~12%. The transverse fluctuations are weakly anisotropic (<delta B_1^2>/<delta B_2^2> ~ 1.1), so the core is a weakly anisotropic Bingham distribution rather than a pure vMF. The broad component is exponential in mu, not in theta, confirming that switchbacks saturate toward mu = -1 rather than decaying away, consistent with the drift-diffusion framework of Bian et al. (2024, ApJ, 960, L15). This physics-based two-population framework connects macroscopic fluid parameters directly to those describing the directional statistics, offering a powerful diagnostic for probing the structural evolution of MHD turbulence and switchbacks in the inner heliosphere.

new.title: Consistently Reproducing Early Galaxy Observations and 21-cm Signal during the Epoch of Reionization
new.summary: In the standard cosmological model, galaxies forming within dark matter haloes are the primary drivers of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). The complex physics of galaxy formation introduces scatter in the relation between halo mass and star-formation activity, with implications for the production and escape of ionising photons. In this work, we implement a stochastic source model in our cosmological radiative transfer simulations. We calibrate our model against the high-redshift ultraviolet luminosity function observed by JWST and observational constraints on Lyman-continuum leakage to constrain the ionising escape fraction. We find that stochastic star formation redistributes ionising emissivity toward lower-mass haloes, producing a more fragmented ionisation topology and delaying the growth of the largest ionised regions relative to the deterministic, observationally calibrated model. However, when the two models match total ionising photon production, their global neutral fractions and 21-cm power spectrum remain nearly indistinguishable, despite small differences in the morphology of individual ionised regions. Additionally, we establish a unified framework that lets us apply source models derived from computationally expensive hydrodynamical simulations (SPICE, FIRE-2 and Thesan) and investigate their impact on large-volume reionisation simulations, extending their prescriptions to scales of >100 Mpc. We find that these prescriptions produce distinct ionisation topologies and 21-cm statistical signatures, even when their global reionisation histories are similar. Our results highlight the importance of combining physically motivated galaxy formation prescriptions from hydrodynamical simulations with large-volume radiative transfer simulations to interpret forthcoming 21-cm observations and constrain the sources of cosmic reionisation.

new.title: Extending SOMPZ beyond Spectroscopic Coverage for Roman Weak Lensing
new.summary: Precision weak lensing cosmology requires accurate galaxy redshift distributions. However, the spectroscopic samples used to characterize these distributions do not fully span the magnitude--color--redshift space of weak lensing source galaxies, necessitating extrapolation. This challenge will be critical at the depth of the Roman Space Telescope's High Latitude Imaging Survey (Roman HLIS). Using simulated LSST Year 4 and Roman HLIS photometry from the Cardinal simulations, we quantify how spectroscopic incompleteness biases photometric-redshift (photo-z) calibration and cosmological constraints. We find that the standard Self-Organizing Map p(z) (SOMPZ) method produces substantial tomographic bin overlaps and biased source redshift distributions. To address these limitations, we develop Roman-SOMPZ, which uses dedicated individual-galaxy photo-z estimators to supply redshift references for tomographic binning and redshift estimation. For the latter, we introduce UMAP-flow-z, an estimator that uses a UMAP embedding of deep-field galaxy colors to infer redshifts for phenotypes lacking spectroscopic representation. Compared with the standard pipeline, Roman-SOMPZ produces better-separated tomographic bins and lower absolute mean-redshift biases in eight of nine bins. Propagating the estimated redshift distributions into cosmological inference, we find that existing spectroscopy is adequate for early-stage weak lensing analyses in the Roman deep fields. Conversely, full medium-tier cosmology will require further improvements in redshift characterization.

new.title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
new.summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.

new.title: Beyond the dust: JWST reveals extinction and ice content in local (U)LIRGs
new.summary: We investigate the spatially resolved extinction and ice column densities in four nearby interacting (U)LIRGs using JWST/NIRSpec integral field spectroscopy (R$\sim$2700; 0.97--5.14 $\mu$m). This wide range encompasses numerous (>25) H recombination and H$_2$ ro-vibrational emission lines, as well as the prominent H$_2$O ($\sim$3.02 $\mu$m) and CO$_2$ ($\sim$4.26 $\mu$m) ice absorption features. We develop three methods to derive phase-specific extinction for ionized (A$_{\text K}^{\text HII}$) and hot molecular gas (A$_{\text K}^{\text H_2}$), and H$_2$O and CO$_2$ ice column densities (N$_{\text H_2O}$ and N$_{\text CO_2}$), exploiting H and H$_2$ emission lines and ice absorption features. Nuclear regions (0.2" radius) exhibit higher extinction and ice column densities than extended regions, with median A$_{\text K}^{\text HII}$ and A$_{\text K}^{\text H_2}$ of 1.25 and 0.75 in the nuclei, compared to 0.61 and 0.50 in the extended regions. The ionized gas is more extincted than the hot molecular gas, with A$_{\text K}^{\text HII}\approx1.5$ A$_{\text K}^{\text H_2}$, while H$_2$O ice column densities are comparable between phases. In some nuclei, continuum-derived N$_{\text H_2O}$ reaches $\sim10^{18.81}$ cm$^{-2}$, likely due to compact obscured components. These results suggest that ionized gas originates in more deeply embedded regions, whereas water ice envelopes both gas phases, with additional ice-rich material around the most obscured nuclei. The median N$_{\text CO_2}$/N$_{\text H_2O}$ abundance ratio is $\sim0.10$, a factor of 2--3 below typical Galactic values.

new.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
new.summary: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

new.title: Microbial Methanogenesis on Mars: A Life Detection Target for an MLE-Type Mission and Future Human Exploration
new.summary: Methane (CH4) is one of the most enigmatic and potentially consequential trace gases detected on Mars, having demonstrated apparent seasonality, localized plumes, or, depending on who you ask, never conclusively detected at all. While the Martian methane mystery remains unsolved, it has sparked a vibrant area of astrobiology research exploring whether microbial methanogenesis -- one of the simplest and most ancient metabolic pathways -- could plausibly proceed under various extreme physicochemical conditions characteristic of the Martian shallow subsurface. The emerging consensus is a cautious but compelling "possibly". These findings elevate methanogenesis as both a top priority candidate biosignature for extant life detection and a justification for urgently advancing in situ instrumentation capable of definitively detecting CH4 and constraining its origin, biotic or otherwise

new.title: Can Blue UV-Bright Galaxies Drive Reionization at Cosmic Dawn? An $M_{\rm UV}=-19.6$ Galaxy with $f_{\rm esc}\approx0.85$ at $z=9.244$
new.summary: We revisit EBG-1, a gravitationally lensed galaxy at $z = 9.244$, using newly obtained deep (14 hr) JWST/NIRSpec G235M ($R \sim 1000$) spectroscopy. EBG-1 is one of the bluest galaxies observed at $z > 9$. Along with its remarkably blue continuum of $\beta = -2.99 \pm 0.15$, we find very weak nebular emission from EBG-1. We obtain a $3\sigma$ upper limit of EW $< 8.4$ Angstrom for C III], a marginal H$\beta$ measurement (EW $= 256.2 \pm 122.2$ Angstrom), and a $5\sigma$ detection of [O III] $\lambda 5007$ (EW $= 882.8 \pm 180.6$ Angstrom). These lines suggest an oxygen abundance of $12 + \log(\mathrm{O/H}) = 7.16 \pm 0.25$ ($\simeq 3\% Z_{\odot}$) and $\log(\mathrm{C/O}) < -0.88$ ($3\sigma$), placing EBG-1 on the C/O-metallicity sequence traced by lower-redshift galaxies. To constrain the escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$), we compare the observed UV slope and emission-line equivalent widths with synthetic spectra generated using BEAGLE. The models favor $f_{\rm esc} \gtrsim 0.75$, with $f_{\rm esc} \approx 0.85$ providing the best overall agreement with the observations. These results suggest that relatively UV-bright galaxies like EBG-1 can achieve the exceptionally high ionizing efficiencies supported by late reionization scenarios.

new.title: The evolution of 3C 306 in the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622: linking spectral ageing, ICM conditions, and jet dynamics through MHD simulations
new.summary: We present a methodology for analysing radio sources in galaxy clusters by combining multi-frequency radio observations, X-ray analysis of the intracluster medium (ICM), and three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, and apply it to the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622 and its associated FR II radio galaxy 3C 306 (IC 4516). The radio emission exhibits a curved structure connecting the lobes, likely indicating a complex dynamical evolution influenced by environmental effects. Spectral index and break-frequency maps reveal a relatively homogeneous radiative ageing distribution, with characteristic spectral ages of $\sim220$ Myr and a smooth spatial gradient. From equipartition arguments, we estimate an equivalent jet magnetic field of $2.1 \pm 0.3\,\mu$G, consistent with values observed in FR II radio galaxies. These observational constraints are used to initialise non-relativistic MHD simulations exploring three scenarios: jet precession, bulk motion of the source through the ICM, and a combined model including both effects. Neither pure precession nor pure source motion alone fully reproduces the observed morphology, whereas the combined model provides a more consistent representation of the jet curvature and lobe asymmetries. Nevertheless, the simulations indicate that source motion is the dominant mechanism shaping the large-scale radio morphology, with jet precession playing a secondary role. The inferred source velocity ($\sim280$ km s$^{-1}$) and precession timescale ($\sim250$ Myr) are compatible with the spectral ageing constraints. These results suggest that the morphology of 3C 306 is influenced by the interplay between jet precession and dynamical interaction with the ICM, highlighting the role of environmental effects in radio-galaxy evolution in clusters.

new.title: A DECADE of Giants: A catalog of 42,000 optically identified galaxy clusters from 13,000 $\mathrm{deg}^2$ of the sky
new.summary: Galaxy clusters are sensitive to a rich variety of physics spanning a wide dynamic range, from microphysical to cosmological scales. Optical datasets are efficient at identifying clusters and studying their properties. We leverage 13,000 $\rm deg^2$ of the sky imaged by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and extract over 40,000 clusters using the redMaPPer algorithm. Our catalog spans $0.2 < z < 0.9$ and $M_{\rm 200c} \gtrsim 10^{14} {\rm M}_{\odot}/h$, with four-band ($griz$) photometric redshifts that have a precision $\sigma_z/(1 + z) \leq 0.008$ below $z < 0.65$, and $\leq 0.011$ between $0.65 < z < 0.9$ and that exhibit an outlier rate of $f_{\rm out} < 0.2\%$. Our cluster finding is calibrated using spectroscopic data, but we find that a larger spectroscopic sample does not improve the performance of our cluster redshift estimation. We cross-match our catalog to those produced from millimeter-wave and X-ray data, and extract scaling relations between various cluster observables. There is excellent agreement between our estimates for different subsets of the 13,000 ${\rm deg}^2$ dataset, and also with results from prior catalogs and simulations. We use our joint analysis of millimeter-wave and optical data to estimate the halo masses of individual clusters. We also provide lensing profiles, measured for each cluster using overlapping galaxy shape catalogs, to enable additional mass-calibration work from the community. We demonstrate from a suite of tests that spatial inhomogeneity in the quality of the imaging data does not have an appreciable impact on the properties of this catalog. We also test a cylindrical richness observable, which is defined such that it is significantly simpler to model, and show that it has precision competitive with the traditional optical richness observable. All data products and measurements are made publicly available.

new.title: Modeling Multi-band Active Galactic Nuclei Lightcurves Using an Self-supervised Attentive Neural Process Network
new.summary: With the the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), observations of tens of millions of quasars are expected. We present a machine-learning framework based on an attentive neural process (ANP) that models stochastic quasar variability and jointly performs two tasks: (i) probabilistic reconstruction of quasar light curves in all six LSST bands, and (ii) inference of physical parameters of the AGN system --- black hole mass, Eddington ratio, and intrinsic variability timescale --- with joint, full-covariance posteriors. The model processes all six bands within a single masked attention mechanism, so that observations in any band constrain the shared driving process, and natively handles irregularly and asynchronously sampled light curves with realistic heteroscedastic noise. We train and evaluate on full ten-year light curves simulated with a relativistic accretion-disk reprocessing model, observed through the fielded Rubin baseline cadence with per-visit photometric noise. The light-curve model is trained with self-supervised, learning from the sparse noisy observations alone and never accessing the underlying noiseless light curves. On a held-out test set, we show that our ANP model reach comparable performances to that of the near-optimal baseline Gaussian process model, while exceeding it in power spectrum reconstruction and damped-random walk timescale estimation. The compact learned latent representation supports future downstream applications, and the fully observation-driven training objective enables direct fine-tuning on real LSST light curves.

new.title: Mass-loss Rates of 74 Bow Shock OB Stars: No Evidence for Bi-stability Behavior
new.summary: Accurate measurements of wind-driven mass-loss rates are essential for understanding the evolution and fate of massive stars. Established techniques for measuring $\dot{M}$ suffer from large dispersions and become insensitive in the regime of weak-winded late-O to early B stars. We employ a promising new technique to measure stellar mass loss for \numstars~early type stars that produce infrared stellar bow shock nebulae. We use updated stellar parameters, improved parallactic distances and proper motions, and modern dust models to characterize the bow shock nebulae and obtain new measurements of mass-loss rates. $\mdot$ ranges from $2\times10^{-9}~\moperyear$ for weak-winded late-O and early B stars at $\log\left(\lstar/L_\odot\right)\approx4.5$ to $4\times10^{-6}~\moperyear$ for the most luminous stars in our sample at $\log\left(\lstar/L_\odot\right)\approx6.3$. Stellar space velocities relative to their local standard of rest are insufficient to accurately reflect the relative star-ISM velocities for the majority of our sample, which have speeds much less than canonical runaway thresholds, suggesting the pervasive influence of bulk interstellar flows in forming bow shock nebulae. Adopting a minimum relative velocity of $20~\kms$ is physically motivated and yields mass-loss rates in excellent agreement with the latest theoretical prescriptions while requiring no adjustable parameters. We find no enhancements in $\mdot$ for stars cooler than 25~kK, in agreement with modern mass-loss recipes that do not include bi-stability effects.

new.title: rapidsim: A Python interface and cross-platform distribution framework for the RAPID protoplanetary disc simulation code
new.summary: The rapidsim is a Python package for the RAPID (Representative Approach for Particle-Integrated Disks) numerical simulation code, which is a modular one-dimensional hydrodynamic simulation code for modelling the evolution of protoplanetary discs and embedded dust particles written in C language. The package was developed to provide a simple and platform-independent tool for launching RAPID simulation without having to manually compile the native code and its external dependencies. rapidsim is distributed through the Python Package Index (PyPI) using pre-built binary wheels for Linux and macOS on both Intel and Apple Silicon architectures and for multiple Python versions. new.title: Intermittent turbulence as the driver of stochastic heating in the near-Sun solar wind
new.summary: Understanding the mechanism by which the energy is dissipated at small scales to heat the outer corona and expanding solar wind, is a primary goal of the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission, and an outstanding question in heliophysics. Recent observational case studies have suggested that the dominant dissipation mechanism(s), stochastic heating (SH) or resonant heating (RH), may be modulated by the Alfvén `surface' ($M_A = 1$), while theoretical and simulation works predict that the mechanism should be modulated by the level of turbulence imbalance. We measure the local energy transfer (LET) rate from $9.8$ to $55$ solar radii from PSP observations, showing that the LET rate peaks at $M_A \sim 0.4 - 0.9$. We connect enhanced LET rates to signatures of intermittency, highlighting the key role that intermittent fluctuations play in heating the near-Sun solar wind. We compare the LET rate with estimates of the SH rate, finding that below $\sim 15$ solar radii the SH heating rate matches the LET rate provided intermittency is accounted for, regardless of $M_A$, while farther from the Sun, SH is unable to account for the observed LET rate. In contrast to predictions by recent theoretical works, this implies that `imbalanced' intermittent stochastic heating may be a viable mechanism to heat highly imbalanced, low-$\beta$ collisionless plasmas, and is likely an important mechanism of dissipation in the outer solar corona and near-Sun solar wind.

new.title: Magnetic-field constraints for four magnetic cataclysmic variables from simultaneous continuum and cyclotron modeling
new.summary: their fields are rarely measured because cyclotron humps must be separated from uncertain continua and assigned to discrete harmonics. We applied a simultaneous continuum-cyclotron analysis to four DESI/LAMOST magnetic-CV candidates. We fit a white dwarf atmospheric model, a hot-spot blackbody, and an isothermal constant-$\Lambda$ cyclotron component in one inverse-variance weighted model. Profiling chi-square over the field strength exposes competing harmonic assignments, which we report as multiple acceptable branches when necessary, and posterior sampling gives branch-conditional uncertainties. We validated the field recovery on EQ Cet, BS Tri, and three SDSS polars, searched 6-7 yr of ZTF photometry for periods and aliases, and used archival UV-to-mid-infrared photometry to bound the donors. The fit gives one robust field, $B = 56.8\pm1.5$ MG, for J0005+2941. J0022+1340 has two indistinguishable branches at $B \simeq 64.4$ and 77.7 MG; J0749+3654 has competitive solutions near 29.3 and 96.4 MG; and J0035+4333 yields an indicative broad minimum at $B = 51.1\pm1.4$ MG. The ZTF data give 105.349 min for J0005+2941, with a narrow eclipse-like minimum, making it a rare eclipsing-polar candidate below the period gap; 80.4062 min for J0749+3654 from double-humped cyclotron beaming; and 143.8 min for J0035+4333. Strong He II 4686 in J0022+1340 and J0035+4333 and flat-to-inverted Balmer decrements in all four support magnetically channeled accretion. Archival mid-infrared photometry excludes donors earlier than about M4.5-M5 V in three systems and M3 V in J0035+4333. Joint continuum-cyclotron fitting gives secure fields when the humps are well resolved and explicit branch constraints otherwise.

new.title: PRIMA prototype spaceflight KID readout electronics laboratory characterization
new.summary: We present further development and testing of prototype kinetic inductance detector (KID) readout electronics for the PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA). PRIMA is a NASA Probe-class astrophysics mission concept with two science instruments, FIRESS and PRIMAger, which provide spectroscopic and polarimetric imaging from 24 to 261 um. Together these instruments will explore the far-infrared sky with spatial-spectral mapping speeds that exceed previous studies by orders of magnitude, opening a vast discovery space. This increase in mapping speed is achieved by densely packed ultra-sensitive KIDs and cryogenically cooled optics. The PRIMA flight readout electronics will use the build-to-print SpaceCube Mini v3.0 which houses a radiation-tolerant Kintex KU060 field programmable gate array (FPGA). A custom high-speed digitizer board is being designed along with an RF electronics (RFE) board. The RFE was designed to provide programmable gain, band filtering, and RF switching between instruments. The prototype readout electronics, including the RFE, use functionally equivalent parts to the flight parts. In this proceeding we measure the readout loopback noise performance in the second Nyquist zone and timestream cross-talk performance. We present preliminary sweeps with the prototype readout coupled to prototype FIRESS detectors. Lastly, we demonstrate a cosmic ray pulse detection and real-time removal with an algorithm implemented in firmware.

new.title: Spiraling into the `snail' cluster MCXC J0157.4-0550
new.summary: We present a deep Chandra (130 ks) study of a striking, tidally induced cold front in a subcluster merging with the galaxy cluster MCXC J0157.4-0550. The subcluster, nicknamed the `snail' (J0157), displays an extensive spiral structure that extends to $\sim 260$ kpc --- one of the largest spiral cold fronts identified to date. Surface brightness and spectral analysis across four sectors reveal a consistent density jump of a factor of $\sim 3$ across the front, together with significant temperature discontinuities, and thermodynamic mapping further delineates the coherent, low-entropy structure of the stripped gas. Unlike classical sloshing cold fronts, the spiral in J0157 arises not from oscillation of a displaced cool core, but from subcluster gas that has been ram pressure stripped and tidally wound into a spiral by orbital rotation. Applying Gaussian Gradient Magnitude filtering and azimuthal surface-brightness analysis, we identify quasi-periodic corrugations along the front consistent with candidate Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instabilities, with a characteristic scale of $\sim 90$ kpc. The presence of these KH rolls constrains the effective ICM viscosity to $\lesssim 0.59$ times the Spitzer value and the magnetic field strength at the interface to $\lesssim 5.9\ \mu$G. These results establish J0157 as a useful laboratory for probing macro-scale merger-induced gas dynamics and micro-scale plasma transport processes in the intracluster medium.

new.title: Numerical estimation of the capture ability of Neptunian mean motion resonances II. Influence of eccentricity and inclination
new.summary: Evaluating the ability of Neptunian mean-motion resonances (MMRs) to capture small bodies is an important step in reconstructing the evolutionary history of the early Solar System. Building on a previous planar model, this study extends the investigation of MMR capture during Neptune's migration to the three-dimensional case, systematically analyzing the effects of the small objects' eccentricity, e, and inclination, i. Through numerical simulations with different migration rates, we obtain the distribution of capture probabilities for 12 MMRs on the e-i plane. The results show that increasing i narrows the ``inevitable capture zone'' (strong MMRs and/or slow migration) and raises the lower e threshold for capture (weak MMRs and/or fast migration), while it may also expand the upper e limit for capture. When the resonance order reaches three, the e-i plane further differentiates into several regions, which are closely related to the types of resonant angles. The emerging i-dominated region, along with its inevitable capture zone, makes third-order MMRs the most likely to benefit from higher inclination, as well as the most likely to host mixed-type resonators. Finally, using a hypothetical planetesimal distribution, we calculated the capture probability and efficiency for each MMR, finding that a cold disk favors strong MMRs, whereas a hot disk reduces differences among MMRs and across migration rates. In the future, a better determination of the population associated with different MMRs and different types of objects will help us understand the dynamical excitation state of the primordial disk in the early Solar System.

new.title: Critical magnetic Reynolds number of the weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo in supersonic plasmas
new.summary: Weakly-collisional plasmas are found in several turbulent astrophysical environments, such as the Intra-galaxy-cluster medium (ICM) and the solar wind, where magnetic fields can be amplified by the turbulent dynamo. The onset of dynamo action is determined by the critical magnetic Reynolds number, ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$, above which turbulent motions amplify magnetic energy. Although ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ has been studied extensively in collisional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, its value in supersonic weakly-collisional plasmas remains unknown. Here we determine ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ using three-dimensional hybrid particle-in-cell (HPIC) simulations of solenoidally driven turbulence with a sonic Mach number $\approx 2$. We vary the magnetic Reynolds number over ${\rm Rm}\approx31$-$1000$ and consider two initial plasma magnetisations, characterised by initial Larmor ratios $r_{\rm Larmor, 0}/L_{\rm box}=1$ and $100$. We find that the magnetic energy grows exponentially at sufficiently large ${\rm Rm}$ and decays when magnetic diffusion dominates at low ${\rm Rm}$. By fitting the magnetic-energy growth rate as a function of ${\rm Rm}$, we measure ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}=190^{+21}_{-17}$ and $198^{+16}_{-18}$ for the initially magnetised and unmagnetised plasma, respectively. These values are the same within their uncertainties, indicating that the initial plasma magnetisation does not significantly affect ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ in the supersonic regime. The measured values are higher than those previously obtained for the subsonic weakly-collisional dynamo, showing that increasing compressibility makes weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo action more difficult to excite. The measured values are also approximately 1.5 times higher than the ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ value reported for supersonic MHD turbulence.

new.title: Prospects for submillimeter VLBI of black hole photon rings with a stratospheric balloon-borne telescope
new.summary: Submillimeter very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) achieves higher angular resolution and probes more optically thin emission near supermassive black holes, with less interstellar scattering toward Sgr A$^*$. Above 345 GHz, however, the atmosphere confines ground-based VLBI to a few high, dry sites. Using 2012-2022 weather, we forecast what a 2.5 m telescope floating at 35-40 km, a successor to the 22 GHz Balloon-borne VLBI Experiment (BVEX) pathfinder, would add to ground-VLBI arrays at 345-690 GHz. The balloon adds little baseline length but reaches higher frequencies, where a fixed baseline is longer in wavelengths. On an ALMA-balloon baseline, Sgr A$^*$ at 460 GHz is at the detection threshold, with ten or more 20 s detections on about half of the simulated April days. These detections lie beyond the polarimetric photon ring transition, where the $n=1$ ring dominates the polarized visibility amplitudes. M87$^*$ at 460 GHz would need frequency phase transfer from a 230 GHz reference to be detected. With phase transfer, most Sgr A$^*$ detections beyond the transition at 460 GHz are on balloon baselines, whose thermal noise meets the linear-polarization threshold within one 300 s scan. At 690 GHz such detections require phase transfer that stays coherent at three times the reference frequency. In Fisher forecasts, a 460 GHz ring-geometry constraint requires balloons but is weaker than at 345 GHz, where balloons add little improvement. High-resolution 460 GHz VLBI science would require a 32 GHz bandwidth backend, submillimeter receivers, and simultaneous 230 GHz reference recording at every station.

new.title: Models of spectral bumps of primary cosmic rays and multi-messenger tests
new.summary: The energy spectra of individual species of cosmic ray nuclei by recent direct detection experiments show complicated structures with spectral hardenings and softenings rather than featureless power laws, which challenge the traditional understanding of the production, acceleration, and propagation of cosmic rays. Particularly, the DAMPE measurements reveal charge-dependent softenings and reject mass-dependent softenings with a high significance. Taking into account the correlated structures at similar energies in the large-scale anisotropies of cosmic rays, one of the most natural interpretations of the spectral structures is the presence of a nearby cosmic ray source. In this case, the softening energies correspond to the acceleration upper limits of such a source, forming the so-called Peters cycle of the spectra. Alternative models such as the injection/acceleration and propagation models may also reproduce the spectral bumps, but show difficulty to explain the anisotropies. Fluxes of secondary nuclei and $\gamma$ rays offer additional tests of different models. Future multi-messenger observations are expected to be able to pin down the origin of cosmic rays.

new.title: Statistical Strong Lensing V. Inference with Microlensed Quasars
new.summary: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars provides direct information on the stellar component of lens galaxies, and can help break the degeneracy between the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and the dark matter. However, a statistical framework to forward model microlensing data while accounting for strong lensing selection effects is still missing. We incorporated microlensing effects into the hierarchical model of Paper III, and investigated to what extent flux measurements of strongly lensed quasars can break the degeneracy between the stellar IMF and the dark matter distribution. We tested the method on a mock sample of 219 doubly imaged quasars, lensed by circularly symmetric lenses. When microlensing effects are modelled, the inference using image fluxes recovers the input foreground population parameters and provides tighter constraints than the inference without flux constraints. The improvement is clearest in the $\mu_\alpha-\mu_5$ plane, where $\mu_\alpha$ describes the mean stellar population synthesis mismatch parameter $\log\alpha_{\rm SPS}$ and $\mu_5$ describes the mean projected dark matter mass within $5\,{\rm kpc}$. The 68% credible interval on $\mu_\alpha$ shrinks from 0.16 dex to 0.09 dex, with the degeneracy between $\mu_\alpha$ and $\mu_5$ significantly reduced. By contrast, fitting the image fluxes without accounting for microlensing leads to large biases on the inferred parameters. This work is a first step towards an accurate modelling of microlensing data. Application to real lens samples will require dropping the circular symmetry assumption and adopting more realistic models for the microlensing magnification.

new.title: Granulation in Color: The Chromatic Stellar Flicker of LTT-9779 and WASP-121
new.summary: Granulation is a persistent feature of stars with outer convective layers and is the photospheric signature of near-surface convective energy transport. In disk-integrated observations, it produces stochastic brightness variations that contribute substantially to stellar variability on timescales of minutes to hours. High-precision, observations with JWST provide an opportunity to study the chromatic signatures of stellar granulation. This work aims to measure the amplitude and characteristic timescale of granulation-induced variability for solar-type stars and to investigate whether the granulation signal shows significant chromatic variation in the near-infrared. We accessed publicly available JWST/NIRISS SOSS time-series observations of LTT-9779 (G7V) and WASP-121 (F6V) and de-trended the light curves by fitting the transits, eclipses, and planetary phase curves. We computed power spectra from the de-trended light curves and fit them with a Harvey granulation profile. We first analyzed the broadband light curves to measure and fix the granulation timescale and then repeated the power-spectrum analysis in individual wavelength channels to measure the chromatic dependence of the granulation amplitude. For LTT-9779, we measure a broadband granulation amplitude of \sigma$=53.8^{+4.1}_{-4.0}$ppm at a timescale of \tau$=4.8^{+1.5}_{-1.3}$min. For WASP-121, we measure \sigma$=59.3\pm4.3$ppm and \tau$=6.3^{+2.1}_{-1.8}$min. We also measure peak oscillation frequencies of \nu$=3382^{+166}_{-191}\mu$Hz and $1649^{+55}_{-69}\mu$Hz in the bandpass-integrated power spectra of LTT-9779 and WASP-121, respectively. In the spectroscopic fits, we find $\sigma$ decreases with wavelength. Our results demonstrate a new observational window on short-timescale stellar variability and provides a way to characterize chromatic stellar noise in transit light curves.

new.title: Newly Identified Planetary Nebula Candidates in M31 using Deep-Learning Search of Hubble Space Telescope Images
new.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has imaged approximately a quarter of a billion stars in M31's disc, yet only slightly over a thousand planetary nebulae (PNe) are known, mostly from ground-based surveys. We show that deep learning can find them in broad-band images alone. In what is the first such search, we scan the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury (PHAT) and the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Southern Treasury (PHAST) mosaics, nearly one square degree of the disk, where a PN is a faint blue point among crowded stars. Because the existing catalogs are incomplete, we train four Faster R-CNN detectors with partial supervision, so that uncataloged PNe are not taught as background, and combine their rankings into one candidate list, an ensemble. On spatially separate test fields, this list places 73% of the known PNe in its top 200, 4 to 6 times the purity of classical color-magnitude selection. Newer detection transformers and segmentation networks trained on the same data do not surpass our detectors. The ranking also follows classifications that the detectors never saw: emission-line objects that the literature calls PNe enter the list at 47%, against 0.6% for those called H II regions, which makes them candidates for reclassification. Among the top 400 candidates, 175 appear in no published catalog, 12 of them flagged as cosmic-ray residuals. One of them, a point source with [O III] emission in nine independent exposures, meets the PN criteria of the three major PN studies of M31, so by those criteria it is a PN. Most of the others lack strong [O III], as expected if narrow-band surveys have found the bright PNe, although some may be PNe with weak [O III]. These results support the near completeness of ground-based surveys for bright PNe and extend it from the PHAT area to PHAST. Finally, we identify evaluation pitfalls for detectors of rare objects and recommend simple remedies.

new.title: Forecasting the Resolvability of Stellar Velocity Dispersions in Ultra-faint Dwarf Galaxies
new.summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs)---the smallest and most dark-matter dominated galactic systems---push the boundaries of our understanding of galaxy formation in the cold dark matter paradigm. As current and near-future imaging surveys continue to expand the known population of extremely faint systems, spectroscopic resources have become a major limitation in our ability to understand the physical nature of these systems. We present projections for the capability of Keck/DEIMOS, Magellan/IMACS, and future spectroscopic instruments (e.g., Magellan/Via and GMT/GMACS) to kinematically distinguish dark-matter-dominated UFDs from dark-matter-free star clusters in the ultra-faint regime. We simulate ensembles of mock observations of ultra-faint dwarf galaxies and apply a formal statistical framework, calibrated to observations, to systematically characterize the ability to resolve velocity dispersions as a function of satellite properties. Our projections suggest that current instruments will struggle to resolve many of systems that will be discovered by the Rubin Observatory. Near future instruments will be capable of resolving a majority of these systems, though they will fail for the faintest and most distant systems. Ultimately, we will require even more advanced instruments, with enhanced stability and velocity precision, to classify the full population of ultra-faint Milky Way satellites.

new.title: Radar and Infrasound Observations of the 2026 May 30 Cape Cod Bay Superbolide
new.summary: Metre-scale impactors connect near-Earth-object dynamics, atmospheric-entry physics and meteorite delivery, but their pre-impact orbits and material properties are rarely measured together, especially for daylight events. We report observations of the 30 May 2026 Cape Cod Bay bolide. A very high frequency (VHF) meteor radar network detected atmospheric-entry plasma, weather radars detected falling meteorites, and infrasound sensors recorded the associated hypervelocity shock. VHF radar range--Doppler measurements resolve the meteor head echo from about 90 to 71 km altitude, while interferometric measurements localize short-lived non-specular plasma wake echoes down to an unusually low altitude of $\sim 30$ km. We identify this as the radar terminus, where breakup is expected to occur. A combined head-echo and trail fit constrains a steep southeastward trajectory over coastal Massachusetts. Weather-radar detections refine the dark-flight solution, place the likely fall region in Cape Cod Bay and constrain probable fragment sizes. Backward propagation of the fitted trajectory gives a heliocentric orbit near the cometary--asteroidal classification boundaries, with conflicting classifications from empirical dynamical criteria. Catalogue comparisons identify no convincing parent body or established meteor-shower association. Regional infrasound independently supports the terminal fragmentation region and yields an energy estimate of 0.5 kt TNT equivalent. The radar and dark-flight evidence are consistent with a dense, mechanically strong meteoroid, possibly iron-rich. The combination of meteor-radar plasma tracking, weather-radar observations of falling meteorites and infrasound measurements can provide accurate orbital elements and trace large meteoroids from atmospheric entry to nearly ground impact.

new.title: Robustness of C/O and mean molecular weight under disequilibrium chemistry
new.summary: Transmission spectroscopy increasingly reduces exoplanet spectra to derived compositional metrics, such as C/O, O/H, and mean molecular weight (MMW), but these quantities do not carry molecular abundance uncertainties in the same way. We assessed the reliability of these metrics for hot Jupiters and sub-Neptunes, by combining analytic uncertainty propagation with photochemical VULCAN forward models and representative published retrieval constraints. Propagating molecular abundance uncertainties produced substantially larger fractional uncertainties in elemental abundance ratios than in MMW. The fractional uncertainties in C/O and O/H were typically comparable to the inferred ratios, whereas the fractional uncertainty in MMW was more than two orders of magnitude smaller in H2/He-dominated atmospheres. Photochemistry and vertical mixing redistributed individual molecules but produced only minor changes in C/O and MMW at the pressures probed by transmission spectroscopy. C/O remains an important diagnostic of atmospheric chemistry and planetary formation history, but its interpretation requires careful uncertainty propagation. Mean molecular weight may provide a comparatively stable population-level diagnostic for linking observable atmospheres to bulk composition, especially across the sub-Neptune radius valley.

new.title: Attitude Estimation of Falcon 9 Rocket Body Based on Photometric Characteristics
new.summary: The proliferation of space debris, driven by increasingly frequent space activities, poses a severe risk to operational satellites and future missions. Consequently, the surveillance and characterization of space objects have become critical. Current methods for attitude estimation of space objects often rely on target-specific models, such as those with a closed set of facets, and typically employ nonlinear filtering or machine learning techniques. However, these approaches often lack general applicability. This study proposes a more general approach to attitude estimation based on photometric light curves. We define a loss function that quantifies the discrepancy between the measured light curve and a theoretical model parameterized by the attitude parameters. By leveraging automatic differentiation to compute the gradients of this function, we use a gradient descent algorithm to achieve rapid and accurate attitude estimation. The proposed method provides a versatile and efficient framework for attitude estimation, overcoming the target-specificity limitations of existing techniques, with the parameters estimation time reduced to 15 seconds and the mean square error lowered to three decimal places. Validation on the third-party database demonstrates that the method exhibits strong generalization capability.

new.title: Galactic warps constrain equivalence-principle violation in the dark sector
new.summary: Current measurements of the expansion of the Universe allow for the presence of evolving dark energy, distinct from a cosmological constant, with an equation of state that seems to violate the null energy condition. One notable explanation for this behaviour is that the dark energy interacts with the dark matter, violating the equivalence principle yet evading conventional laboratory and astrophysical constraints. Such models produce fifth forces acting only on dark matter. We show how such forces separate halo and stellar disk centres, creating a potential gradient across the disk that warps it into a cup shape. Measuring the warps of $4\times10^3$ edge-on disks in Sloan Digital Sky Survey images and modelling the fifth-force signal together with competing baryonic effects, we find no sign of the predicted correlation between the measured warps and the fifth-force field. This constrains the fifth-force strength relative to gravity to $\Delta G/G_N<7.7\times10^{-4}$ at 95% credibility (or $<1.7\times10^{-3}$ once systematic uncertainties are included) for force ranges of 8 Mpc and above. In the infinite-range limit of a scalar rolling today, even the conservative bound is three times stronger than the tightest cosmological bound (which, unlike ours, depends on the scalar's cosmological evolution) and about two orders of magnitude below other astrophysical bounds. It disfavours at 2-3$\sigma$ the couplings preferred by recent fits of interacting dark energy to cosmological data unless gravitational screening is invoked.

new.title: Clumpy Outflows from Super-Eddington Accreting Black Holes. II. Conditions for Clump Formation
new.summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) commonly exhibit ultra-fast outflows (UFOs) with velocities of $0.03$--$0.3~c$. Recent high-resolution X-ray observations with XRISM/Resolve suggest that UFOs may have a clumpy structure. However, the formation and evolution of these clumpy outflows remain poorly understood. In the first paper of this series, we investigated the formation of clumpy outflows using numerical simulations and find that sufficiently high spatial resolution is required to reproduce clumpy structures numerically. In this second paper, we perform a series of numerical experiments to identify the key physical processes governing clump formation. We find that spatial fluctuations of physical quantities at the disk surface are essential for the formation of clumpy outflows, whereas spatial and temporal fluctuations at the inner boundary have only a minor effect. Furthermore, density structure-function analysis suggests that the high-density regions have an elongated morphology with characteristic transverse widths of several tens of $R_{\rm g}$, possibly produced by radiation Rayleigh--Taylor instability. A more comprehensive investigation of the instability in general-relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, where accretion disk structures emerge self-consistently, is expected to provide deeper insights into the physical origin of clumpy outflows.

new.title: Gravitational filtering, magnetic-field inhomogeneity and Coulomb collisions in a kinetic model of a plasma atmosphere with stochastic heating at its base
new.summary: We investigate the effects of stochastic heating, magnetic inhomogeneity, and Coulomb collisions in coronal loops using a reduced kinetic model. Coulomb collisions thermalize suprathermal populations generated by intermittent heating and populate velocity-space regions inaccessible from the lower boundary in the collisionless limit. We consider two regimes: when heating varies faster than the electron crossing time, the plasma develops a multitemperature nonthermal distribution; when it varies more slowly than the proton crossing time, individual heated loops approach an isothermal state. In the collisionless limit, conservation of the magnetic moment restricts the accessible velocity space, producing a strong temperature anisotropy, with parallel temperature exceeding perpendicular temperature, and additional density depletion. We find that Coulomb pitch-angle scattering efficiently suppresses these effects under typical coronal conditions. In the short-time-scale regime, density and temperature profiles approach those obtained with a constant magnetic field, while gravitational and collisional filtering sustain the temperature inversion. In the strongly collisional long-time-scale regime, magnetic-field-induced anisotropy is nearly eliminated, and individual loops remain approximately isotropic and isothermal. An increasing temperature profile then emerges only after averaging over unresolved flux tubes with different temperatures. Thus, Coulomb collisions largely suppress the macroscopic kinetic signatures of magnetic-field inhomogeneity in the transition region and low corona.

new.title: Inverse-designed tapers to improve throughput of on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs
new.summary: Astrophotonics offers a pathway towards compact and stable spectrographs for future large telescopes. The size of these spectrographs does not scale with the diameter of the telescope aperture; thus, they offer a cost-effective way to achieve astronomy science requirements compared to traditional optical spectrographs. A major limitation of current on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs is the significant loss incurred at interfaces between distinct components, particularly at the input and output fiber interfaces, limiting overall throughput. In this work, we investigate inverse-designed architectures to optimize transitions between these components to improve throughput. Inverse design formulates device design as an optimization problem, enabling non-intuitive geometries that can achieve high performance. We focus on optimizing coupling between an arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) spectrograph and an input single-mode fiber. Our approach explores two classes of fabrication-constrained inverse design. The first is shape optimization, which optimizes the geometry of the boundary of a coupling taper. The second is topology optimization, which optimizes the material distribution in a design region to gradually transform the optical mode between components. Both methods are implemented using the Tidy3D package from Flexcompute. We use germanium-doped silica for the core of the photonic components and silica as the cladding, and we use an SMF-28 fiber as input. This work demonstrates a pathway to improve astrophotonic spectrographs through computational inverse-design methods. Leveraging higher throughput, we can improve signal-to-noise ratios offered by photonic devices and position ourselves to design high-performance, cost-effective instrumentation for the next generation of telescopes, both on the ground and in space.

new.title: V347 Aurigae: from Peak to Quiescence
new.summary: We present an analysis of eight epochs of high-resolution optical spectra of the YSO (young stellar object) V347 Aur. The source exhibits periodic brightness variations spanning $\sim$2 mag over several months, interpreted as cyclic accretion-burst and quiescent phases, making V347 Aur a useful probe of the broad range of accretion and outflow variability in YSOs. When faint, V347 Aur shows an M-type photospheric absorption spectrum; when bright, it exhibits a strong emission-line spectrum. Our Keck/HIRES spectroscopy was obtained during the decay of an accretion burst. The emission spectrum includes the strong H I, Ca II, and He I transitions commonly seen in YSOs, as well as numerous weaker metal lines, for which we provide a complete inventory. As the star fades, photospheric absorption lines deepen, consistent with decreasing veiling from the accretion continuum. H I and He I emission, which trace accretion, strengthen relative to the continuum as it fades, but show the expected decline in strength with decreasing accretion after correcting for the strong early veiling. Ca II behaves similarly, with line profiles that alternate between red- and blueshifted dominance, which we interpret as the rotation of the magnetospheric accretion flows. Narrow, slightly blueshifted absorption in Ca II, Na I, and K I indicates disk winds with localized density enhancements. Forbidden [O I] and [S II] emission is blueshifted, with broad shoulders and low- and high-velocity narrow peaks, consistent with a disk geometry that obscures much of the receding outflow. Their behavior as the continuum fades is similar to that of the broad accretion lines. The V347 Aur system is a useful proxy both for the ubiquitous short-term accretion variability observed in YSOs, and for their secular evolution on longer time scales.

new.title: Mid-infrared Imaging of SR 12 c with JWST/MIRI: Grain Growth in an Evolved Circumplanetary Disk
new.summary: The physical properties of circumplanetary disks offer insights into the formation of giant planets and their satellites. The circumbinary planetary-mass companion SR 12 c (1200 au from SR 12 AB) hosts an isolated dust disk directly detected with ALMA. We present JWST/MIRI imaging of SR 12 c from 5.6 to 21 $\mu$m and analyze its spectral energy distribution from infrared to submillimeter wavelengths. Phenomenologically, the dust disk can be described by a two-component blackbody with large contrasts in characteristic temperatures and radii. Physically motivated models with varied geometries and heating mechanisms suggest a predominantly flat, irradiation-heated disk with a smaller contribution from viscous dissipation. The disk is inferred to be compact, with an inner radius of ~3 $R_{\rm Jup}$. The outer radius is only loosely constrained, with a characteristic value of ~3 au. The lack of strong 10 $\mu$m excess emission suggests significant grain growth and dust settling. We also find that SR 12 c is broadly consistent with the empirical star-disk scaling relations, providing context for its possible formation pathway. These results demonstrate the power of combining mid-infrared and submillimeter observations with disk modeling to better understand the physical properties of circumplanetary disks.

new.title: The Impact of an AGN on PAH Spectral Features in Galaxy Evolution Simulations: Continuum Dilution and Excitation of PAHs
new.summary: Galaxies hosting an active galactic nucleus (AGN) show diminished power and non-standard spectral feature ratios from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) compared with normal star-forming galaxies. Proposed mechanisms for this difference include a combination of AGN-driven PAH grain processing, differential heating from the surrounding radiation field, and continuum dilution. These potentially competing factors are difficult to disentangle observationally. In this paper, we investigate the impact of the AGN radiation field on the excitation properties and potential dilution of the mid-IR emission features via constrained numerical experiments of idealized galaxies in simulations that include a self-consistent model for the evolution of dust. We find that, for the integrated spectrum of our simulated Milky Way analog and independent of grain-processing physics, the apparent PAH emission is progressively diminished as AGN luminosity is increased. For spectra within the central half kiloparsec, PAH features are entirely obfuscated when an AGN of any sampled luminosity is present. We additionally find that the UV radiation from an AGN is capable of impacting PAH band ratios, though note that we do not yet include a model for potential photodestruction of PAHs. Our model suggests that the inferred lack of PAHs via featureless mid-IR spectra from galaxies hosting AGN may simply owe to the direct continuum from the AGN overpowering mid-IR features from PAHs in the ISM of the host galaxy. Future work will investigate the relative role of AGN continuum dilution and PAH heating vs photodestruction/ionization of PAHs.

new.title: Long-term ultraviolet variability of Taurus T Tauri stars from the IUE archive
new.summary: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from Classical T Tauri stars, generated primarily by magnetospheric accretion, plays a fundamental role in circumstellar disk evolution. However, its long-term variability remains poorly characterized due to the scarcity of homogeneous time-series observations. We investigate the variability of the near-UV continuum and the Mg II resonance doublet to assess whether both diagnostics trace the same underlying accretion variability. We analyzed the complete archive of long-wavelength International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) observations of T Tauri stars in Taurus-Auriga, comprising 475 low-dispersion spectra of 36 objects collected over 18 years. We characterized continuum variability using three windows between 2600 and 3100 Angstroms and examined continuum-subtracted Mg II fluxes, UV-V colors, and Lomb-Scargle periodograms to investigate correlations and characteristic timescales. Continuum fluxes between 2675 and 3055 Angstroms are strongly correlated, with variability dominated by changes in continuum level rather than spectral shape. Near-UV and quasi-simultaneous optical fluxes are significantly correlated in six of the seven best-sampled sources, although their relative variability differs. The Mg II-continuum relationship shows substantial object-to-object diversity, ranging from correlated variations with different fractional responses to decoupled or anti-correlated behavior, indicating no universal temporal response. Lomb-Scargle periodograms reveal formally significant features in some well-sampled objects, including near 10 and 33 days. However, irregular and clustered sampling prevents their identification as reliable periodic or characteristic timescales.

new.title: An Enhanced Intersecting-Lines Method for Optical Loss Characterization in SIS Heterodyne Receivers
new.summary: Accurate knowledge of radio-frequency (RF) losses in front of superconductor--insulator--superconductor (SIS) mixers is essential for optimizing millimeter- and terahertz heterodyne receivers. However, such losses are difficult to extract from conventional hot/cold-load measurements because the measured receiver noise combines contributions from the input optics, the mixer, and the intermediate-frequency chain. In this work, we present a numerical implementation of the straight-line, or intersecting-lines, method for estimating input-referred RF noise and optical loss from standard Y-factor measurements. Hot/cold IF spectra are acquired while sweeping the local oscillator (LO) pumping level from under-pumped to over-pumped operation, so that each IF frequency bin gives a family of linear relations between receiver output power and input load temperature. We evaluate all pairwise intersections between these lines and analyze the crossing cloud to obtain the effective RF input noise. We repeat the analysis across the IF band and multiple LO tunings which provides a frequency-resolved characterisation of the input losses over the full band. Our implementation turns the straight-line technique into a reproducible framework for receiver characterisation and relative optical-loss comparison in low-loss front-end configurations.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: LO-pumped characterization of the SIS heterodyne mixer used in this work. The figure shows the SIS current, I SIS I_{\mathrm{SIS}} , and the IF output power, P IF P_{\mathrm{IF}} , as functions of the SIS bias voltage, V SIS V_{\mathrm{SIS}} , for different LO pump levels. new.title: Impact of Residual Gain Errors on the Detectability of Ionized Bubbles during Reionization with SKA 21-cm observations
new.summary: Detecting ionized bubbles and characterizing their properties and the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM) using the HI 21-cm signal provides direct probes of cosmic reionization. Here, we focus on the detection of individual ionized bubbles around luminous sources using a matched-filter technique. We investigate the impact of time- and frequency-correlated residual antenna gain errors on the detectability and characterization of individual ionized regions with SKA-Low. We simulate mock SKA-Low AA* observations that include the HI 21-cm signal, astrophysical foregrounds, residual gain errors, and system noise corresponding to 100 h of observing time. We subtract the foreground components from the gain-corrupted data and subsequently apply the matched-filter technique to the residual visibilities. We find that the matched-filter technique is able to detect the ionized bubble and constrain its properties in the presence of residual gain errors with the rms amplitudes up to $\sigma_A\sim1\%$ and rms phases up to $\sigma_\phi\sim1^\circ$. Residual gain errors at similar levels prevent the reliable identification of ionized regions in reconstructed HI 21-cm images and bias the estimated HI 21-cm power spectrum. Furthermore, we find that increasing the temporal correlation length increases the level of gain-induced artifacts in the reconstructed image. In contrast, increasing the frequency correlation length reduces these artifacts, as some fraction of the spectrally smooth gain-induced residuals is removed during foreground subtraction. We further find that the inferred bubble and IGM parameters remain largely unaffected by residual gain errors, although their uncertainties can increase. These results demonstrate the potential and robustness of the matched-filter technique for detecting and characterizing individual ionized bubbles in the presence of substantial residual calibration errors.

new.title: Tidal Disruption Events in Active Galactic Nuclei: Thermal Radiation and Jets
new.summary: Over the past decade, dozens of Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) have been identified, with many more expected from upcoming surveys. A small subset has been observed to launch transient, highly luminous relativistic jets, for which the origin of the requisite magnetic flux has not been identified. A non-negligible fraction of TDEs are expected in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), where a magnetized accretion flow is already present. As shown first by Chan et al. (2019), the collision of a TDE debris stream with this flow can substantially alter both disk and debris dynamics, leading to a possibly Eddington-limited flare. Here, we use the Athena++ radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code to simulate the time near peak fallback rate of a TDE in an AGN, studying the debris-disk interaction, the radiation emitted, and the accumulation of magnetic flux near the horizon. In the example simulated, the accretion rate climbs to $\sim 12\,\dot{M}_{ \rm Edd}$, while the escaping solid angle-integrated luminosity approaches $\sim L_{ \rm Edd}$. The photon luminosity is strongly asymmetric, brighter in the hemisphere from which the debris strikes the disk and dimmer in the hemisphere toward which the debris travels. The photon spectrum peaks in the EUV. The polar magnetic flux grows $\sim 33$-fold, enough to raise the Blandford--Znajek luminosity by a factor $\sim 10^3$, reaching a level sufficient to power observed TDE jets. The polar magnetic flux is also asymmetric, likely making any jet similarly asymmetric, but in the opposite sense to the photon flux.

new.title: A 4-20 GHz Superconducting 90deg Hybrid Using Capacitively Loaded Coupled Lines for 2SB Heterodyne Receivers
new.summary: We report the design and cryogenic characterisation of a broadband superconducting 90deg intermediate-frequency (IF) hybrid covering 4 to 20 GHz for sideband-separating (2SB) heterodyne receivers. The hybrid is implemented in thin-film niobium using capacitively loaded edge coupled transmission lines, avoiding the air-bridge interconnections required in Lange-coupler layouts while retaining a compact superconducting implementation with low loss and good quadrature balance. Cryogenic measurements using Vector Network Analyser (VNA) show amplitude and phase imbalance better than 0.6 dB and 6deg, respectively, across the full band. When used in a 2SB receiver, this level of IF balance is consistent with the observed image-rejection performance in the 10-20 dB range, for the full receiver. The design supports the development of wide-instantaneous-bandwidth 2SB receivers for millimeter and submillimeter observatories, improving spectral grasp for broadband line surveys and high-redshift line searches.

new.title: Single-Transit Parameter Estimation with Calibrated Uncertainties
new.summary: The growing volume of photometric data from current and upcoming exoplanet surveys demands automated analysis pipelines to detect and characterize exoplanet transit signals. Among these, single-transit events present a challenge, since only one event is observed, and standard transit-fitting techniques for periodic signals do not directly apply because they rely on phase-folding. Beyond detection, characterizing these events is equally critical for follow-up, yet existing approaches are either sensitive to stellar variability and require prior detrending, or depend on stellar priors and per-target fitting. This work presents a convolutional neural network that predicts transit depth, duration, and mid-transit time, together with calibrated uncertainties, directly from a single transit signal. Our network is trained on synthetic light curves and evaluated against a trapezoidal least-squares baseline. On 120 confirmed exoplanets, both methods achieve comparable median errors, but the baseline fails to locate the transit in 10% of cases, producing unreliable estimates that would propagate into follow-up prioritization. In contrast, our network fails in only 1% of cases, yields lower mean absolute errors, and does not require detrending or stellar priors. Detrending would distort or remove the transit along with high stellar variability, precisely where the baseline fails and our network succeeds. Finally, we identify 169 new transit candidates in TESS Sectors 27-60 and apply our approach to obtain their physical parameters, creating a catalog that includes single-transit, multi-transit and multi-planet systems. This approach offers a scalable path toward automated characterization of single transit events, a population that will grow with upcoming surveys.

new.title: The Star Formation Histories of Different Components of M31's Halo from Photometric Estimates of Fe and $α$ Abundances
new.summary: We present the chemical-abundance distributions and star-formation histories of the M31 halo components using photometric Fe and $\alpha$ abundance estimates derived from the PAndAS broad-band $g$ and $i$ filters and the Subaru/HSC $NB515$ narrow-band filter. We selected about 76,400 candidate M31 giant stars and constructed a synthetic photometric training dataset based on model isochrones. We estimated elemental abundances and errors using random forest regression models. We identify various halo components, including about 32,500 stars in the ``smooth" halo (where ``smooth" refers to the complete sample with all the known substructures removed), and infer their star-formation histories from comparisons of their abundance distributions. From the radial abundance gradients, we find that [Fe/H] decreases while [$\alpha$/Fe] increases toward the outer halo. Including substructures further enhances the radial abundance contrast, suggesting that the smooth halo stars are accreted at relatively early times, before the progenitor galaxies produce large numbers of Type Ia supernovae. Both M31 and the Milky Way show similar radial gradient trends, but M31 exhibits higher [Fe/H] and lower [$\alpha$/Fe] values overall, suggesting that the smooth halo of M31 may possess a larger fraction of relatively younger stars associated with more recent merger events. Future photometric observations with additional narrow-band filters and larger spectroscopic samples are expected to provide a better understanding of the formation and evolution history of M31.
